query: I have a 76‑year‑old female inpatient with acute pancreatitis. Among female inpatients aged 71–81 with acute pancreatitis, compute medication complexity score over the first 72 hours, stratify into tertiles, and report LOS, in‑hospital mortality, and 30‑day readmission rates per tertile.
final_sql: SELECT p.gender, p.anchor_age, p.anchor_year, p.anchor_year_group, a.admittime, a.dischtime, a.deathtime, s.los, s.in_hospital_mortality_rate, s.readmission_30_days_rate, m.medication_complexity_score, t.tertile, row_number() OVER(PARTITION BY t.tertile ORDER BY m.medication_complexity_score DESC) AS rank_within_tertile FROM patients p JOIN admissions a ON p.subject_id = a.subject_id JOIN stay s ON a.stay_id = s.stay_id JOIN emar m ON m.subject_id = p.subject_id AND m.hadm_id = a.hadm_id JOIN (SELECT subject_id, hadm_id, tertile FROM patients WHERE gender = 'F' AND anchor_year_group BETWEEN 71 AND 81) AS t ON t.subject_id = p.subject_id AND t.hadm_id = a.hadm_id WHERE p.gender = 'F' AND p.anchor_age = 76 AND p.anchor_year = 2019 AND p.anchor_year_group BETWEEN 71 AND 81 AND a.admittime BETWEEN 0 AND 72;
